deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is page 2 ('Mathematik') of a printed 1863 antiquarian sales catalogue: the 'Catalog des Antiquarium's von W. Setzer in Bremen' (see the previous page, which carries the title and the date 1863). Its ink stamp, 'Ermanno Loescher, Librajo, Via Carlo Alberto 5, Torino', shows through mirrored. The page continues the alphabetical list of mathematics books for sale from Wagner to Wolf. Each entry gives author, short title, format, place, year (with the leading 1 omitted, e.g. 799 = 1799), binding, and price in Silbergroschen (Sgr), sometimes with the original price in Thaler in parentheses. Examples are Wiegand's school textbooks, Wolf's 'Elementa matheseos universae', Wittstein's logarithmic tables and 'Prismatoid', Weisbach's tables of sines and cosines, and Weißenborn's 'Die cyclischen Curven'. The most mathematically notable title is A. Wichert's 'die 5 und 17 Theilung der Lemniskate', on dividing the lemniscate into 5 and 17 equal parts. This is the Gauss–Abel theory of lemniscatic division, the analogue of constructing regular polygons. There are no handwritten annotations, calculations or derivations by Riemann. The sheet was presumably kept among his papers (Riemann died in 1866) as a book catalogue he received or consulted, possibly with an eye to purchases. The only quantitative content is the pricing. For example, 'Wiegand, Lehrbuch d. eben. Trigonometrie … 3 Sgr' carries the note '(15 Exem. zu 1 Thlr 6 Sgr.)'. Using 1 Thaler = 30 Sgr (my assumption, the standard Prussian rate of the period), that is 36 Sgr for 15 copies, or 2.4 Sgr per copy as a bulk discount.

results.modern_name: Lemniscatic division / complex multiplication of the lemniscatic elliptic function (Abel's theorem on lemniscate division)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed book catalogue with no annotations or mathematics by Riemann. Its presence in his papers is only of minor biographical or bibliographic interest.

checkable.asserts: Bulk offer '15 Exem. zu 1 Thlr 6 Sgr' (assuming 1 Thlr = 30 Sgr) gives 12/5 = 2.4 Sgr per copy, below the single-copy price of 3 Sgr.
5 and 17 are Fermat primes, the cases in which lemniscate division is constructible by ruler and compass (Abel), relevant to the Wichert title.

transcription_corrections: The Thaler sign in the image is a ligature symbol (rendered '₰' on the previous page). The transcription's 'Thlr' is an interpretive substitution.
'Hbldrbd.' (Wagner, H. A. E. entry) should read 'Hlbldrbd.' (Halblederband), as in the image.
'exoctaëdro' in the Wezel entry is printed run-together but means 'ex octaëdro'.
The header line on the previous page reads 'No. 16 / 155 ↓ 162 = 8 Bl.' This is an archival foliation note for the catalogue sheets (folios 155–162), not mathematics.
